steps.scene: You're turning left into a side road. Two people have already stepped off the kerb and are walking across it.

options.text: Steer round behind them, leaving plenty of room
Give way and let them finish crossing
Sound your horn so they know you're turning in

question.explanation: People already crossing the side road have priority. Wait — don't hurry them with the horn, your lights or your engine.

steps.title: A clear road isn't the whole check
steps.body: Turning right with nothing coming the other way? People waiting to cross that side road still come first. Give way before you turn in.

question.prompt: Nothing is coming, but people wait to cross the side road. What do you do?

options.text: Turn in — they're safe where they are on the pavement
Wave them across so you can get on
Wait and give way to them

question.explanation: Give way to anyone crossing, or waiting to cross, the road you turn into. Never wave them over — you can't see what's behind you.

steps.scene: Street repairs have closed the left-hand pavement ahead, and barriers funnel people off it towards the kerb.

question.prompt: What is that cue telling you?

options.text: Keep your speed up to get clear of the works quickly
Expect people walking in the road — slow right down
Nothing changes; pedestrians have to wait for traffic

question.explanation: A closed pavement pushes people into the carriageway. Pass slowly and leave them room.

steps.title: Walkers on a country lane
steps.body: With no pavement, people are told to walk on the right so they face the traffic. On a lane, that means they come towards you on your side.

question.prompt: On a country lane with no pavement, where do you expect walkers?

options.text: Coming towards you, on your side of the road
Ahead of you with their backs turned, on your left
On the verge only — they never walk on the road

question.explanation: Expect walkers head-on, and expect to meet them late on a right-hand bend. Ease off and give them width.

a.label: A white stick
a.body: The person is blind. They may have no idea your car is there until they hear it.

b.label: A white stick with a red band
b.body: The person is deaf as well as blind. Your horn tells them nothing at all.

question.prompt: A pedestrian carries a white stick with a red band. What does it mean?

options.text: They're blind — the band is only a reflective strip
They have limited mobility
They're deaf and blind

question.explanation: Red band means deaf and blind. Sounding your horn achieves nothing — wait, and give them all the time they need.

steps.title: A dog in a coloured coat
steps.body: A dog in a yellow or burgundy coat is trained to help a deaf person. Its owner may never hear you approaching.

question.prompt: You see a pedestrian with a dog in a burgundy coat. What does it tell you?

options.text: The dog is in training and the owner is its trainer
The pedestrian is deaf
The pedestrian is an older person

question.explanation: Yellow or burgundy coat means a hearing dog. Don't count on engine noise or a horn to be noticed.

steps.scene: You're first in the queue at a pelican crossing. Your light turns green, but two older people are only halfway across.

options.text: Edge forward and rev gently so they get a move on
Flash your lights in case they haven't seen you
Wait patiently until they're clear

question.explanation: Older or disabled people often need far longer than you'd expect. Green means go only once the crossing is clear.
